source.title: Simply B1 Preliminary for Schools: 8 Complete Practice Tests
source.questions: Original student-book pages supplied by the user.
source.answerKey: WordHop-authored answer key and English explanations based on the supplied recordings; not a publisher key.

parts.title: Part 1
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

questions.prompt: Which programme will they watch first?

optionText.B: A cooking programme showing a chef.
optionText.C: A recycling programme showing children collecting cans.

questions.explanation: The cookery programme comes first, before the recycling programme at nine. The football match is much later.
questions.evidence: I really want to watch my favourite cookery program first.

questions.prompt: Why did the boy go to bed late?
questions.explanation: He stayed up finishing a difficult maths project. His mother suggests television, while painting was his friend George’s work.
questions.evidence: We had a difficult project on maths, and it took a lot of time to finish it.

questions.prompt: What did the girl see at the science museum?
questions.explanation: She saw the old computers. The car exhibition was closed and she did not reach the mobile-phone section.
questions.evidence: I’ve never noticed how different and huge old computers were before.

questions.prompt: How much was the restaurant bill?
questions.explanation: The £95 amount is what his father paid after the discount. £20 was deducted, so it must not be subtracted from £95 again.
questions.evidence: My father paid £95. ... The amount of money I told you before was after that discount.

questions.prompt: Which book will the girl borrow from her friend?

optionText.A: A book with a heart on the cover.
optionText.B: A book with an aeroplane flying around a globe on the cover.
optionText.C: A book with a police officer on the cover.

questions.explanation: She accepts the story about a police officer because she wants action. Travel books are her usual reading, and she rejects the assumption about romance.
questions.evidence: It has a great story about difficult situations a police officer has to deal with every day. It sounds perfect.

questions.prompt: What did the girl cook?

optionText.A: A ring-shaped cake with fruit beside it.

questions.explanation: She baked a cake. Pizza was an abandoned plan, and Jade brought soup made by her mother.
questions.evidence: Then I decided to bake a lovely cake.

questions.prompt: Which animal did the boy enjoy seeing best?
questions.explanation: The birds were his favourite animals on this particular trip. Cows are his general favourites, while the rabbits came second this time.
questions.evidence: The birds in the trees were the most attractive animals for me this time.

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.

questions.prompt:
You will hear a boy talking to a friend about his grandma’s house.

What does the boy like most about it?
questions.explanation: He values being able to walk there quickly and being close to school. He would not have chosen the colours, and the house is small.
questions.evidence: I can walk there in 10 minutes ... My grandma’s house is next to my school.

questions.prompt:
You will hear two friends talking about a birthday present for their friend, Mary.

What do they decide to do?

optionText.A: buy her cinema tickets for the weekend
optionText.B: ask her brother what music she likes
optionText.C: tell Mary to choose her birthday present herself

questions.explanation: They decide to ask her brother Jack for advice about concerts she would enjoy. Cinema is mentioned as an interest, not their final present choice.
questions.evidence: Her brother, Jack, could give us some suggestions. ... I am going to see Jack this afternoon after class and ask him what he thinks.

questions.prompt:
You will hear two friends talking about a concert.

What do they agree on?
questions.explanation: Both agree that too many tickets were sold and there was not enough room to move. They disagree about the volume and do not object to expensive tickets in principle.
questions.evidence: They sold more tickets than they should have done. I was thinking the same thing.

questions.prompt:
You will hear two friends talking about a party they went to.

What happened?

optionText.A: Too many people came to the party.
optionText.B: The house was in a mess after the party.

questions.explanation: Peter’s parents returned a day early and found the forbidden party. There were only ten guests and the house was not very dirty.
questions.evidence: I’ll never forget the look on his face when they came home a day early.

questions.prompt:
You will hear two friends talking about a competition.

The girl feels

optionText.A: sad that she can’t share the prize with the person she really wants to.
optionText.B: disappointed that her friend didn’t win a prize as well.
optionText.C: proud of herself but unhappy that her parents can’t travel with her.

questions.explanation: She is sad that the rules require her to take her parents, so her friend cannot share the prize trip. Her parents can travel with her.
questions.evidence: I have to go with my parents, so I can’t take you.

questions.prompt:
You hear two friends talking about a new student.

What does the boy say about the student?
questions.explanation: The boy thinks the new student is quiet and finding it hard to meet people. He describes her as interesting rather than boring or unfriendly.
questions.evidence: She seems to be a little bit quiet.

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instructions: For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one or two words or a number or a date or a time.
parts.heading: Julie’s trip to Venice
parts.context: You will hear a student called Julie talking to her class about her trip to Venice.

questions.prompt: You can use bus, ________ or boat to go to Venice from the airport.
questions.explanation: Train is the third transport option alongside bus and boat. The sentence already includes the other two.
questions.evidence: You can either go by train or bus from the airport.

questions.prompt: Julie and her parents started their journey to Arsenale at ________.
questions.explanation: They set off at 10.15 and arrived at 11.30. The question asks for their departure time.
questions.evidence: We set off at 10.15 and we arrived there at 11.30.

questions.prompt: The museum card costs £________.
questions.explanation: The museum card cost £30. £20 is the cost of the separate three-day boat ticket.
questions.evidence: We also bought a museum card for £30.

questions.prompt: Julie’s favourite place to walk was over ________.
questions.explanation: She most enjoyed walking over Venice’s bridges and watching boats below. The plural “bridges” matches the recording.
questions.evidence: The thing I enjoyed most was walking over the many beautiful bridges.

questions.prompt: The best food to eat in Venice is ________.
questions.explanation: She calls fish the nicest food to eat in Venice. Pizza and pasta restaurants are common but are not her recommendation.
questions.evidence: The nicest thing to eat in Venice is fish.

questions.prompt: Julie’s parents bought some ________ for her relatives.
questions.explanation: Her parents bought toy boats for the cousins. Julie herself bought sweets, so those are not the answer.
questions.evidence: My parents bought some toy boats for our cousins.

parts.title: Part 4
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.context: You will hear an interview with a young basketball player called Isabella.

questions.prompt: Why did Isabella start to play basketball?

optionText.A: She didn’t have someone at home to play with.
optionText.B: Her parents who worked at a court encouraged her.
optionText.C: There were many basketball courts near her house.

questions.explanation: Her parents worked long hours, so she needed an activity while they were away. There was only one small court nearby.
questions.evidence: My parents used to work many hours every day, so I had to find something to do.

questions.prompt: Why does Isabella think she is such a good basketball player?
questions.explanation: She attributes her ability to spending her time outside playing repeatedly. Her talent developed through practice rather than being described as innate.
questions.evidence: I stayed outside and I played and played and naturally I became really talented.

questions.prompt: Who was the first to tell Isabella that she could play basketball as a professional?
questions.explanation: Her school teachers first noticed her ability, and one persuaded her parents to support her. Her parents were told about her potential afterward.
questions.evidence: My teachers noticed how good I was. ... One of my teachers told my parents that I could do really well in my sport.

questions.prompt: What was Isabella most proud of?
questions.explanation: Her proudest moment was leading the team into the opening ceremony while carrying the flag. She says this mattered more than winning the medal.
questions.evidence: I got to hold the flag to lead our team around the stadium ... That was actually the proudest moment.

questions.prompt: What are Isabella’s plans for the future?

optionText.B: to take part in the Olympics

questions.explanation: She wants to study hard and enter university, possibly to become a doctor. She is unsure about pursuing an Olympic medal next.
questions.evidence: I want to study hard and enter university.

questions.prompt: In ten years from now Isabella will definitely want to be
questions.explanation: She is certain she wants to be successful and happy, whichever career she chooses. Being a doctor or a basketball player remains undecided.
questions.evidence: To become a successful, happy woman, either as a doctor or as a basketball player.
